literal: Hostility he-will-not-see prosperity when-coming; it increasing he-will-see ruin to-bring-about.
translation: When prosperity is on its way, a person will not entertain hostility; but to bring about his own ruin, he will seek to increase it.
modern: ஒருவனுக்கு நல்வாழ்வு வரும் காலத்தில் அவன் பகைமையை விரும்ப மாட்டான்; அவனுக்கு அழிவு வரப்போகிறது என்றால் அந்தப் பகைமையை மேலும் வளர்த்துக்கொள்வான்.
explanation: This couplet connects a person's inclination toward conflict with their impending fortune or downfall. The phrase 'ஆக்கம் வருங்கால்' (when prosperity comes) indicates that a mind destined for success naturally avoids enmity. Conversely, when ruin is imminent ('கேடு தரற்கு'), a person is drawn to escalate conflicts, actively seeking the increase of hostility. The poet illustrates that the choice to ignore or amplify discord is the very mechanism that brings about wealth or destruction.
